subject: KV-store & prompt-output sanitization — execution plan and confirmation
messages:
From: Kepler Health <security@keplerhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: AcmeCloud Compliance <security@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: remove KV cache entries + prompt/output logs (Kepler customer dataset)

Hi Hannah,

Per our regulatory review (state-level healthcare retention limits), we need Redwood to securely remove all prompt inputs, generative outputs, and KV cache entries tied to Kepler customer IDs prefixed with "KLP-2023" across the hosted instance in us-west-2. Scope: prompt_inputs, generated_outputs, request/response logs, and any cached KV shards that may contain PII-like tokens.

We also need a short execution plan, expected start/end time window, and verification artifacts (manifest + redacted log snippets) for our auditors. Prefer completion within the week if feasible.

Thanks,
Asha Patel
Security Lead, Kepler Health
security@keplerhealth.com

Attachments: export_manifest_request.csv (list of sample keys we provided)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Kepler Health <security@keplerhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: remove KV cache entries + prompt/output logs (Kepler customer dataset)

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear scope. Today: quick acknowledgement and a few clarifying questions so we can provide an accurate plan.

1) Confirming scope: do you want us to remove only runtime KV shards (ephemeral cache) and persisted prompt/output logs stored in our S3 buckets, or also remove artifacts from any snapshot backups we may have taken?
2) Any specific retention exception windows (e.g., legal hold for a subset of IDs)?
3) Preferred maintenance window? We can schedule a 2-hour gated operation during off-peak (US evening) to minimize user impact.

We will prepare an execution plan and manifest template and loop in Marissa (security/compliance) and Diego (ops) to run the sweep. Expect a follow-up with start/end ETA and a link to the evidence folder.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Manager, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
---
Redwood Inference | hannah.schmitt@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

From: Kepler Health <security@keplerhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, AcmeCloud Compliance <security@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: remove KV cache entries + prompt/output logs (Kepler customer dataset)

Hannah —

Thanks for the quick reply. Confirm: remove runtime KV shards + persisted prompt/output logs in Redwood-managed S3 buckets and any short-term backups (snapshots) created in the last 90 days. No legal holds on the IDs we listed.

Preferred window: start Monday nightly maintenance (we understand this is outside your IMMEDIATE window — if you can begin tonight in a gated read-only mode that's ideal).

We also require a signed attestation after completion (DocuSign is fine).

Regards,
Asha

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Kepler Health <security@keplerhealth.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: KV-store & prompt-output sanitization — execution plan and confirmation

Hi Asha / Hannah —

We stood up a short, auditable plan:
- Window: 2028-06-30 22:00 — 2028-06-30 23:30 PDT (gated, can abort).
- Steps:
  1) Create isolated sweep job in a non-production staging runner with identical config and a dry-run to collect affected keys.
  2) Produce sweep_manifest_20280630.csv listing keys/objects identified.
  3) Execute deletion in Redwood S3 buckets and issue cache invalidation across edge nodes.
  4) Run snapshot scan for last 90 days and remove any matched snapshot objects; record deletion record.
  5) Generate redacted log snippet(s) and final sweep_proof_bundle.tar.gz for client download.
- Rollback: we will not perform any data restoration; instead we will produce an immutable audit record and the raw deletion manifest.

Attachments: sanitization_playbook_v1.pdf (playbook + verification checklist)

Action items for Kepler: please confirm acceptance of the scheduled window and an authorized signature via the DocuSign link. Once we receive sign-off, Diego will coordinate the run and post evidence to the Drive folder.

—Marissa
Principal, Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Kepler Health <security@keplerhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: KV-store & prompt-output sanitization — execution plan and confirmation

Asha / team —

Worked through the sweep runbook during the gated window. Summary:
- Start: 2028-06-30T22:00:12-07:00 
- End: 2028-06-30T23:08:47-07:00
- Objects identified: 4,132 keys (sample recorded in sweep_manifest_20280630.csv)
- Actions taken: deleted persisted prompt_output objects, removed matching S3 snapshots from last 90 days, invalidated KV cache shards across the regional cluster, and trimmed ephemeral runtime shards.
- Evidence: sweep_log_snippet.txt (redacted), sweep_proof_bundle.tar.gz (contains checksums + deletion receipts), sanitization_playbook_v1.pdf (procedure).

We'll upload the evidence bundle and send the DocuSign attestation immediately. Please reply-all to confirm acceptance and close the ticket.
